openings.claim: Extra downward corner compression is supposedly necessary for lateral retention. A possible counterexample transfers sideways load through removable edge stops while removing that extra compression; neither retention implies tight compression nor tight compression implies retention.
openings.delta: Use the four strips as two bolted, rubber-protected rim clips, with removable keeper portions beside and above opposite hatch edges. Adjust clearance without forcing the left corner downward. Slide both clips completely clear for opening; tether recoverable components with cord. The changed dependency is lateral edge bearing instead of added seal friction from corner pressure.
openings.prediction: Nearest rival: the same clips retain the hatch mainly because downward preload increases seal friction. Edge-bearing restraint predicts at most 1 mm displacement under 20 N with light preload and no induced opposite-corner lift. The friction rival predicts deterioration when extra preload is removed. These are prospective observations, not established performance.
openings.probe: First check whether supplied strips can capture the existing rim and hatch without modification. Within ninety minutes fabricate only if that geometry permits. Allocate twelve closure/pull trials: two ordinary tightened closures, one with the right-contact card; then ten removal-arm opening cycles, final closure disturbed. Measure marked-position deviation, apply the supplied 20 N scale pull, time reopening by one technician, and inspect seal tears each cycle. Observe corner lift as a discriminating mechanism measurement. Fit all observations within twenty minutes.
assumptions: Rim underside access, hatch-edge clearance and keeper removal paths are unspecified; inaccessible geometry defeats this construction.
Pads and strip contact can protect the hatch, rim and seal without permanent deformation; this requires inspection.
Clip grip and strip stiffness must transmit 20 N without slip or excessive bending; supplied dimensions do not establish capacity.

Reject the counterexample if any candidate cycle exceeds 1 mm displacement or thirty seconds reopening, produces a new tear, obstructs the opened inspection area, or fails the disturbed closure. Stop before damage if tightening threatens a hard constraint; an incomplete probe establishes no outcome.

assessment: One tentative removal operation. Geometry and capacity remain indispensable unknowns, so no feasible counterexample or deployment is demonstrated. Avoiding extra compression alone does not establish seal stability.
